how: Written by hand each quarter (see RUNBOOK, 'Next-quarter backdrop'). Start from the evidence: XBI and sub-sector moves this quarter, rates, financing and M&A data, our net-supply read, the catalyst calendar, and policy news. Then make one call per What-worked dimension: the group to favour, the group to avoid, and why in one or two sentences. The dashboard shows each group's 2025-26 record next to the call; a call may go against the record if the backdrop has changed, but it must say why.
backdrop: Biotech gave back ground this quarter: XBI hit a five-year high (~$170) in August, closed Q3 near $158 and is about $140 now. In Q3 clinical-stage names fell 11% while commercial-stage names rose 4.5%, so the market has been paying for revenue over risk.
The Fed raised rates 25bp in September and the market expects more; higher rates hurt long-duration, cash-burning small caps most.

M&A is still the main source of liquidity: $39B of deals in Q3 and 40 deals over $1B this year, a record; public takeovers handed shareholders an estimated $17B of cash in Q3. Since 1Q25 cash back from takeovers has exceeded new equity raised every quarter.
Supply is rising: 49 companies have gone public this year (IPOs, reverse mergers, SPACs) and follow-ons stay heavy around data, so investors are asked to fund more names.
January brings the J.P. Morgan conference, year-start guidance and a dense first-quarter readout calendar; historically deals and catalysts cluster early in the year.

stage.why: Acquirers keep paying for late-stage, de-risked assets, and Ph3/filed names beat the market in 7 of 8 quarters; early-stage names need cheap money, which a rate hike and heavy supply take away.

size.why: $1–5B names led by 10 points last quarter; most 2026 takeouts were $1–10B companies and specialists own about 30% of these, so takeover cash recycles here first. Micro caps lagged by 10 points and are the most exposed to rising rates and dilution. Large caps (+22% last quarter) are the defensive alternative.

mom.why: Moderate winners beat the market in 6 of 8 quarters and again last quarter; stocks already down 40%+ lagged by 7 points last quarter, and with money tightening, broken stories tend to keep falling until they raise or restructure.

px.why: Higher-priced names led by 14 points last quarter and are where institutions can build positions; sub-$2 stocks lagged by 12 points last quarter (their 2025–26 record is mixed, 4 of 8) and face reverse splits, delisting notices and toxic financing when money tightens.

mod.why: Antibodies have beaten the market the last two quarters (record 4 of 8) and big pharma keeps paying for them in immunology and oncology (e.g. AbbVie/Apogee, $10.9B); cell therapy beat the market in only 1 of 8 quarters on manufacturing cost and slow launches. We are not following the vaccine group's 5 of 8 record into 1Q27, given US vaccine-policy uncertainty.

nov.why: Novel mechanisms with clinical data have held their premium (6 of 8 quarters), and late entrants in crowded classes lagged on every 4-quarter hold.

cl.why: I&I beat the market in 6 of 8 quarters and has the deepest pool of big-pharma buyers and late-stage readouts in 1Q27; neuroscience beat it in 2 of 8 and lagged on every 2-quarter hold, as it depends on binary readouts with high failure rates. Oncology (2 of 8) is a close second to avoid.
